body: For a configuration-lifecycle task, bind the selected module entry and actual stage source. Independently observe creation, application-context environment registration, language change, color-mode change and destruction. Require the accepted source to pass and wrong-entry/wrong-event mutations to fail their declared intended checks. Read raw worker observations rather than trusting startup completion or producer booleans. These verified controls cover only the recorded operator-dispatch source seam; separately calibrate actual framework delivery, ArkTS/HAP, exact emulator API and ohosTest before qualifying the task.
title: A startup-only observation does not establish configuration delivery through the selected stage

body: Use exact AST facts and cross-file import/call evidence to trace responsibilities from product shells through feature modules into common services. Preserve unresolved dispatch and runtime behavior as explicit gaps; syntax success is not a behavior proof.
title: Code Workshop responsibility analysis

body: Treat this checkout as one multi-product Harmony application. The root build profile composes common, feature, and phone/PC/TV/wearable product modules. Inventory every tracked source before narrowing; do not infer whole-repository semantic coverage from the existing selected-path case Skills. Reassess through the generic evidence flywheel and use emitted dimension gaps to target later analysis rounds.
title: Code Workshop repository boundary

body: Mine iterative cohorts only after binding an owning module, cross-file responsibility chain, editable/context paths, and an independent Oracle hypothesis. Treat the 480-scope structural partition as routing evidence, not behavior readiness. Existing debounce, feedback, image, loading, cache, and ArkWeb families are calibration evidence, not permission to skip unexplored modules. Preserve rejected candidates and use coverage or Oracle gaps to select the next Skill refresh; shared imports alone are never cases.

The purchaseData example flow is exact only through a bounded local chain; object identity, external HMS behavior, reachability, exception flow, and callback ordering remain unresolved.

The IAP package contains TypeScript/compiled JavaScript, Cordova metadata and hooks, an Android Java bridge, type declarations, and Cordova/Ionic examples. Reassess through the generic evidence flywheel; bind the verified purchase flow only to its three evidenced layers and retain the package build failure as a gap rather than operation proof.

body: Mine iterative cohorts across structurally distinct bridge concerns: action routing, request mapping, Task success/failure conversion, activity-result handling, hooks/plugin installation, declarations versus runtime exports, and example integration. Require a repaired build/test contract before promotion because the package build script currently invokes tsc without inputs or a root tsconfig. Preserve that blocker as round evidence, continue behavior analysis that does not depend on the build, and resume qualification from the exact parent round once the contract is repaired.
title: Cordova HMS IAP diversified seed policy

body: Partition facts by sample root before building call, state, lifecycle, or native bridge graphs. The repository mixes ArkTS, TypeScript, C++, resources, and generated/editor artifacts. Report parser exclusions and unresolved references per project so one noisy sample cannot contaminate another.
title: Guide Snippets project-partitioned analysis

body: Treat guide-snippets as a corpus of independently buildable sample projects, not one application. Establish the owning sample root from its nearest root build-profile before interpreting module facts. Repository-wide counts measure corpus coverage; build and test claims must be per sample root. Reassess through the generic evidence flywheel and close per-project behavior gaps rather than extrapolating one sample across the corpus.
title: Guide Snippets corpus boundary

body: Use iterative cohorts for breadth, project-boundary discovery, and false-positive suppression. A candidate must stay inside one declared sample unless a source-to-source cross-sample dependency is proven. High-cardinality SDK imports such as ArkUI or hypium are routing signals, not difficulty evidence. Measure newly behavior-ready and Oracle-ready sample scopes each round, preserve rejected candidates, and drive the next round toward distinct mechanisms instead of repeatedly sampling familiar imports.
title: Guide Snippets seed and noise policy

body: The consumable path is query environment, recover unfinished purchases, decode purchase data, verify/deliver through an application-server seam, then finish the purchase. Exact local dataflow to iap.finishPurchase is supported; external SDK signature, server verification, account state, and callback scheduling remain runtime contracts.
title: Harmony IAP purchase lifecycle

body: Treat the exact 44-file checkout as one Harmony entry application. The application has nine ArkTS files and four product-type pages; the tracked source contains no test suite. Keep later injected ohosTest assets separate from upstream repository knowledge. Reassess through the generic evidence flywheel; the verified consumable flow advances only its explicitly bound scope and cannot stand in for the other product pages.
title: Harmony IAP client boundary

body: Do not keep mining only purchaseData. Run iterative cohorts across environment readiness, product query, consumable recovery/finish, non-consumable ownership, subscription lifecycle, navigation, JWS parsing, and performance/reliability boundaries. Every promoted case requires upstream-aligned ohosTest or device observables plus wrong-variant discrimination. Retain failed build, emulator, Oracle and ambiguity results so the next round refines the responsible Skills rather than repeating the same path.
title: Harmony IAP diversified seed policy
